title: The Perry Como band
summary: Terry Snyder, Stanley Webb and others in the Como band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Some of these great bands, these commercial

bands, I remember one band that you were in, I mean, every musician in there to me was like the epitome of a musician, that was the Perry Como band. I remember Bob Haggart was the bass player. Name some of the guys in that band.

That was a good band. Had Willy Roland on the piano, Terry Schneider on the drums. Terry Schneider was probably the busiest drummer in New York, and probably the most worried drummer in New York. An insecure fellow, he died of colitis, a massive heart attack, and everything just fell apart all at once, literally.
He was working around the clock.
Around the clock. Now, other people worked around the clock but they didn't get that kind of reaction. But he was very insecure about his ability, he really didn't know how good he was, I guess.
Because I thought he was fantastic. I had the opportunity to play with him and nobody could -- he could do anything.
Yes, he could. And he could do it well, too.
Little tiny bit of a guy.
Yeah, I can just picture him. And, let's see, --
The guitar player?
Well, at first it was Alan Reuss, and
Perry Como brought in a friend of his that used to play with an orchestra, the Ted Weems Orchestra, Danny --
Danny Perry.

Danny Perry, yeah. And as you say, Bob Haggett on the bass. We had Bobby Burns, came in on the trombone section. For a while we had Lou McGarity in there. Bob Alexander. We had Stanley Webb in the sax section.
That was really The band.

Yeah, he was probably Mr. Commercial Saxophone. He could play all the doubles perfectly. There's a man that practiced. Before he got that busy he would practice each instrument. He had about six instruments, he practiced 12 hours a day, you know, two hours each instrument. English horn, oboe, clarinet, all the saxophones. Bass clarinet. And you'd always see Stanley, that was another small guy, wiry --
With the big bass baritone sax and bass sax.
Yeah, armloads of instruments.
Always at least 45 minutes ahead of time, he'd be there --
Well, he had to warm everything up. Yeah, it seemed like all the best musicians in the dance bands all would come out and go into the commercial field.
Well, they could read well and they could
do well.
